subject: Post-call: CareWell logging controls & PII redaction pilot
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@carewell.health>, CareWell Security <security@carewell.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: CareWell logging controls & PII redaction pilot

Hi Emily / CareWell team —

Thanks again for the run-through today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we agreed would help us scope a pilot: 

- Scope of logs: you confirmed interest in request/response capture (application payloads), HTTP headers (including custom tracing headers), and downstream error traces from the API gateway. Please confirm whether you also want LB/access logs included.
- Sensitive fields: you mentioned patient identifiers (MRN), SSNs, and free-text notes. Please share a short sample of the most common endpoint payloads (sanitized) or a schema.
- Retention target: you said compliance prefers short retention for PII; we need to confirm target TTL (30/90/365 days) for audit and for non-PII telemetry.
- Residency: you requested US-only storage (us-east-1). We can provision a Private pilot with that region pinned.
- Redaction approach: our proposed options are (A) ingest-time pseudonymization (hash/HMAC for trace IDs, tokenization for fields), (B) field-level redaction with allowlist of headers, or (C) full payload redaction with sampled exceptions for debugging. We recommended (A) or (B) for minimal impact to debugging while reducing PII exposure.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
1) CareWell to send a short list of 5 representative endpoints + 2 sample payloads (sanitized) and the retention policy target.
2) Redwood to draft a scoped pilot plan (2 weeks) that runs in a customer-dedicated sandbox and demonstrates ingest-time redaction + retention enforcement.
3) Define success criteria: 1) no raw PII stored in logs, 2) trace IDs are non-reversible, 3) latency impact <10% at 95th percentile.

I attached a one-pager for the pilot scope and a quick sketch of the redaction flow we discussed. Happy to jump on a short call next week to finalize the pilot window.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pilot-scope.pdf (PDF), redaction-design-sketch.png (image)

Thanks Sean — helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side before we share samples: 

1) Scope: we do want application payloads + headers + gateway traces. LB logs are lower priority for the pilot, we can exclude them initially.
2) Retention: our compliance leads are currently leaning toward 90 days for telemetry that may contain pseudonymized identifiers, and 365 days for system-level audit logs. We will confirm once the security team reviews your pilot plan.
3) Trace IDs: the ask from legal is that trace identifiers are not reversible to a user identifier — hashing/salting is acceptable if it’s proven non-reversible.
4) Data residency: us-east-1 is required.

I’ll circulate a sanitized example payload and a short compliance note from our security team (security@carewell.health) by EOD Monday. Also including a link to our SOC2 page in case you need it for integration docs.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call: CareWell logging controls & PII redaction pilot — technical proposal

Sean / Monica —

Following the call and Emily's note, I sketched a technical approach for the pilot that keeps production fidelity while minimizing PII risk. High level: ingest-time scrub -> pseudonymize -> TTL-backed retention -> encryption-at-rest. Key points: 

- Ingest-time scrubbing: we run a lightweight pipeline in front of our telemetry store that applies an allowlist for headers (keep standard HTTP headers + X-Correlation-*), and an explicit denylist/regex for common PII patterns (SSN, MRN, emails). Example regex (simplified): "\\b\\d{3}-\\d{2}-\\d{4}\\b" for SSN; we will iterate with samples.
- Trace IDs: we recommend HMAC-SHA256(trace_id, tenant_salt) -> store truncated 128-bit hex to preserve linkability without reversibility. Tenant_salt is stored in customer KMS if requested. This satisfies non-reversible requirement from legal.
- Field tokenization: for user text (free-form notes), option to run a PII detector and replace matches with stable tokens (token:user_XXXX) so that debugging across requests is possible without exposing raw values.
- Retention enforcement: TTL on log objects; deletion job runs hourly; audit events capture deletion operations. We can support 30/90/365 day windows per stream.
- Residency & keys: pilot runs in a dedicated private deployment in us-east-1. We support customer-managed KMS for encryption; otherwise Redwood-managed keys with strict access controls.
- Debugging path: where necessary we can implement an exception workflow for on-demand targeted retrieval with an approver flow (legal sign-off).

For the pilot we propose: 
- Pilot scope: 3 production-like endpoints, ~48 hours of traffic replay (sanitized), verify redaction rules against sample payloads, validate latency impact with load tests.
- Deliverables: redaction rules file, HMAC salt management plan, retention/TTL config, runbook for emergency unredaction (manual, audited).

I attached a draft rules file I’d like to iterate on once we get the sample payloads. Happy to walk through this on a tech call with Emily/security.

-Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redaction-rules.yaml

1) CareWell will send: 3 representative endpoint schemas + 2 sanitized payload samples, and confirmation on retention targets (you mentioned 90 days for pseudonymized telemetry).
2) Redwood will provision a us-east-1 dedicated sandbox and populate it with the redaction rules Karthik attached; we'll run a 48-hour replay and a load test to measure latency at P95.
3) Success criteria: no raw PII persisted, trace IDs HMACed with tenant salt, retention TTL enforced, and a short runbook for ad-hoc investigations.
4) Proposed pilot dates: Oct 2–Oct 13 (2 weeks). Can you confirm availability for a kickoff on Oct 1?
